Codebooks of the BDHS recode files

Source: R/data.R
bdhs_codebook.Rd

Variable-level metadata of the BDHS recode files: name, label, type, number of value labels and number of non-missing values, so you can see which variables exist in which round without the data, and compare rounds. Value labels are in bdhs_value_labels.

Usage

bdhs_codebook

Format

A tibble with 25,910 rows (one per variable per file) and 9 columns:

survey_id

DHS survey identifier.

recode

Recode/file type, e.g. "KR" (see bdhs_recodes()).

file_stem

DHS file name the metadata describe, e.g. "BDKR7RFL".

position

Position of the variable in the file.

variable

Variable name (lower case).

label

Variable label as in the file (typographic quotes made ASCII).

type

R class of the variable when read with haven: "haven_labelled" (numeric with value labels), "numeric" or "character".

n_value_labels

Number of value labels (rows in bdhs_value_labels).

n_valid

Number of records with a non-missing value. DHS special codes such as 9/99 ("missing") or 8/98 ("don't know") count as non-missing; system-missing values and empty strings do not. Compare with the number of records of the file to see if a variable was asked of everyone.

Source

Metadata extracted from DHS recode files (Stata format) by data-raw/03-build-codebooks.R; the files used are listed in data-raw/codebook-sources.csv. Labels are the work of The DHS Program/ICF and the survey implementing agencies.

Details

These are metadata only: no data values, ranges, frequencies or observed codes are included. They were extracted from files the maintainer is licensed to use, so only the following rounds and recodes are covered:

  • KR (children under 5) for 1993-94, 1999-2000, 2004, 2007, 2011, 2014, 2017-18 and 2022;

  • every 2017-18 file: BR, FW, HR, IR, KR, PR, SQ and VA;

  • IR, KR and PR for 2022.

1996-97 and the SPA and BMMS surveys are not covered. Variable names are lower case, as returned by bdhs_read().

See also

bdhs_value_labels, bdhs_variable(), bdhs_search(), bdhs_harmonized_vars().

Examples

# Which rounds have a KR caesarean-section variable (m17)?
bdhs_codebook[bdhs_codebook$variable == "m17" & bdhs_codebook$recode == "KR",
  c("survey_id", "label", "n_valid")]
#> # A tibble: 8 × 3
#>   survey_id label                          n_valid
#>   <chr>     <chr>                            <int>
#> 1 BD1994DHS delivery by caesarian secti-na       0
#> 2 BD2000DHS delivery by caesarian section     6812
#> 3 BD2004DHS delivery by caesarian section     6901
#> 4 BD2007DHS delivery by caesarian section     6150
#> 5 BD2011DHS delivery by caesarean section     8753
#> 6 BD2014DHS delivery by caesarean section     4493
#> 7 BD2017DHS delivery by caesarean section     5299
#> 8 BD2022DHS delivery by caesarean section     5331

# Variables of the 2022 PR about anthropometry
pr <- bdhs_codebook[bdhs_codebook$survey_id == "BD2022DHS" &
  bdhs_codebook$recode == "PR", ]
head(pr[grepl("^hc7", pr$variable), c("variable", "label")])
#> # A tibble: 4 × 2
#>   variable label                                     
#>   <chr>    <chr>                                     
#> 1 hc70     height/age standard deviation (new who)   
#> 2 hc71     weight/age standard deviation (new who)   
#> 3 hc72     weight/height standard deviation (new who)
#> 4 hc73     bmi standard deviation (new who)
